---
title: "Dissections"
subtitle: "Every plot can carry the evidence behind it — one keypress away, never in the way"
---

A figure panel is a verdict: *caloric intake predicts body weight*. The evidence behind that
verdict — twenty per-subject curves, the model comparison you didn't show, the ANOVA table —
usually lives in a scratch folder far from the figure, or nowhere at all. **Dissections** give
that material a home *attached to the plot itself*.

# The folder convention

Any plot in `plots/` can own a dissection folder named after it under `plots/_dissections/`:

```
plots/
├── growth.svg                      # the composed panel
└── _dissections/
    └── growth/                     # ← growth.svg's dissections
        ├── overview.svg            #   loose files form the default group
        ├── by_subject/             #   a subfolder is a named group (a tab in the viewer)
        │   ├── subj01.svg …
        └── _stats/
            └── anova.csv           #   CSVs/TSVs open as sortable tables
```

The name mirrors the plot's path under `plots/` (so `plots/models/fit.svg` owns
`plots/_dissections/models/fit/`), with the extension dropped. Pasted images and PDF snips
work too — they're keyed by their file name.

That's the whole contract. There is no manifest and no registration: **the folder is the
API**. Your analysis script (or an agent) drops files in. Flux can create a dissection folder
and write the text notes you edit there; it leaves your images, tables and other files alone.

# What goes in

Anything that explains the plot. Typical dissections:

- **Breakdowns** — one panel per subject / session / condition behind a summary plot.
- **Alternative analyses** — the same question answered another way (different model,
  different normalization), kept honest next to the version you published.
- **Statistics** — `_stats/` CSVs with the tests behind the asterisks.
- **Notes** — one or more `.txt` files with observations, decisions and searchable tags.
- Images of any kind (**svg**, **png**, **jpg**, **webp** — fluxplot outputs included) and
  **csv**/**tsv** tables are first-class in the viewer; other files are listed by name.

Dissections are deliberately **out of the way of composition**: nothing under `_dissections/`
turns up in an ordinary plot-gallery search, lands in a figure by accident, or
rides along into an export. They are context, not content.

Out of the way is not locked away. In the importer, type **`_`** and the reserved folders
(`_dissections`, and `_lighttable` if the project has one) appear as rows you can enter with
**Enter**. Inside one, searching only looks *within* that folder, so you can find a
per-subject panel and insert it deliberately — **⌫** steps back out to the ordinary `plots/`
search.

# Viewing them

**Beside the canvas, live.** The sidebar's **Plots** view ([The Plots rail](../modes/figure.qmd#the-plots-rail),
**Alt+G**) shows the dissections of whichever plot you last clicked — in its gallery or on
the canvas — and follows each new click. Tables come first as small previews, then each
folder of panels. Clicking a placed per-subject panel shows its siblings (the folder it came
from). With a file selected, clicking another plot that has a file of the same name keeps it
selected in the same place, so you can flip between plots and compare one subject. The pin
holds the pane on one plot while you work elsewhere.

**Full screen.** In the figure editor, select a plot and press **D** (or click **Dissections** in the
Inspector — it shows a count). The viewer opens full-screen, and the **⧉** button shrinks it
to a floating window you can keep beside the canvas:

- **Arrow keys** move through the grid; **[** / **]** change the column count; **1–9** switch
  group tabs.
- **Enter** expands a file. Images zoom at the cursor with **Ctrl+scroll**, pan with
  **Space+drag** or plain scroll, and toggle fit/1:1 with **Enter**. CSV/TSV files open as
  tables with a sticky header — click a column to sort, numeric columns right-align.
- **Esc** steps back: detail → grid → closed.

The viewer is live: files dropped into the folder while it's open simply appear.

# Notes and finding plots

In the sidebar's Dissections pane, switch from **Files** to **✎ Notes**, or click **✎ Notes**
in the full viewer, then **+ Note** to create a text file. Give each note a name; Flux adds
`.txt` if needed. Select a file to edit it; double-clicking a `.txt` among a plot's files opens
it here too. Notes save as you type and when you leave the field; **Ctrl+S** saves immediately.
A failed save keeps your draft, and an external edit is reported instead of being overwritten.
The text files remain readable in any editor.

In the gallery search, turn on **Notes** to search note contents across every plot in the
project. For example, `#TODO` finds that tag wherever you wrote it. Each result shows the
plot, note, line and the matching text; click it to select that plot and open the note in the
Notes pane below. Switch **Notes** off to return to searching plot names.

To browse folders, click **Folders** in the Dissections pane or press **Alt+/** (from anywhere
in Figure or Slide; it opens the Plots view if needed). The lower
pane becomes a searchable folder tree with the number of plots under each folder. Click a
folder (or use **Arrow keys** and **Enter**) to show only its plots; choose the top folder to
see everything again. Press **Alt+/** again, or **Esc**, to restore Dissections. The chosen
folder stays in place while you switch the sidebar to Layers and back. Companion
collections such as `_dissections` stay out of this tree.

Plot previews use the same readable background in the sidebar, Space preview, fullscreen
gallery and Dissect viewer: each image sits on its own page. Transparent dark text sits on
paper; light text sits on a dark surface. An image's own background remains part of the image.

For scripts and agents, `flux list-dissections [plot]` prints a plot's groups and files (or,
with no argument, every plot that has dissections) — see the
[CLI reference](../reference/cli.qmd).

# Troubleshooting

- **Pressed D and got "select a plot"** — Dissect works on a selected plot or image (or a
  drilled part; the part's owning plot is used; with several selected, the last plot you
  added). Group selections don't map to one dissection folder.
- **The Plots view says "Library plots have no dissections"** — plots from your global plot
  library live outside the project; dissections belong to a project's `plots/_dissections`.
- **The viewer says the folder doesn't exist** — nothing has created it yet. The empty state's
  **Create dissection folder** button does it, and shows the exact path.
- **Renamed a plot?** Flux never renames files in `plots/`, so rename the matching folder
  under `plots/_dissections/` yourself — until you do, the plot reports no dissections
  (nothing breaks, and the folder is never deleted).
- **A file shows as a name card with no preview** — images and CSV/TSV files have previews;
  `.txt` notes open in the text editor. Other files remain listed by name.
- **A note won't save** — text notes are limited to 1 MiB and cannot follow symbolic links.
  If another editor changed the file, copy any draft text you want to keep, then choose
  **Discard draft and reload** to read the disk version before editing again.
